Hadhrat Abdur Rahmaan bin Auf (RA) and Hadhrat Uthmaan (RA) both said, "O Rasulullaah ﷺ! We fear that the Quraysh may suffer an attack from Sa'd." Rasulullaah ﷺ then said, "O Abu Sufyaan! Today is a day of mercy. On this day shall Allaah give honour to the Quraysh." Then he sent a message that Hadhrat Sa'd (RA) be relieved of the post (as flagbearer) and assigned the task of bearing the flag to Hadhrat Qais (RA) (Hadhrat Sa'd's son). (In this way) Rasulullaah ﷺ intended that the flag would really not leave the hands of Hadhrat Sa'd (RA) when it went to his son (and he would therefore not feel offended). However, Hadhrat Sa'd (RA) refused to surrender the flag until he received a signal from Rasulullaah ﷺ. Consequently, Rasulullaah ﷺ sent his turban to Hadhrat Sa'd (RA), by which he acknowledged the command and handed the flag over to his son Hadhrat Qais (RA). [^1]

Hadhrat Abu Layla (RA) who reports that they were with Rasulullaah ﷺ when he informed them that Abu Sufyaan was at a place called Araak. The Sahabah (RA) then went there and captured him. With their swords still sheathed, they surrounded him and brought him before Rasulullaah ﷺ. Rasulullaah ﷺ said to him, "Shame on you, O Abu Sufyaan! I have brought to you the world as well as the Aakhirah. Accept Islaam and live in peace."
Hadhrat Abbaas (RA) had been a friend of Abu Sufyaan, so he said, "O Rasulullaah ﷺ! Abu Sufyaan loves glory, so grant him some." Rasulullaah ﷺ therefore sent a crier to Makkah to announce, "Whoever locks his door shall be safe! Whoever throws down his weapons shall be safe! Whoever enters the house of Abu Sufyaan shall be safe!" Rasulullaah ﷺ then sent Abu Sufyaan with Hadhrat Abbaas (RA) and they both sat at the edge of the valley. When the Banu Sulaym tribe marched by, Abu Sufyaan asked, "Who are they?" "They are the Banu Sulaym tribe," replied Hadhrat Abbaas (RA). Abu Sufyaan then said, "What have I to do with the Banu Sulaym tribe?"
Thereafter, Hadhrat Ali bin Abi Taalib (RA) came at the head of the Muhaajireen. It was when Rasulullaah ﷺ arrived amongst the Ansaar that Abu Sufyaan asked, "O Abbaas! Who are they?" Hadhrat Abbaas (RA) said, "They are the red death (people unafraid to spill the blood of their enemies). That is Rasulullaah ﷺ with the Ansaar." Abu Sufyaan commented, "I have seen the kingdom of the Kisra and the kingdom of the Caesar but I have never seen anything like the kingdom of your nephew." Hadhrat Abbaas (RA) said, "This is (not a mere kingdom but the greater kingdom of) Nabuwaat." [^2]

Hadhrat Urwa (RA) narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ left (Madinah) with an army of twelve thousand comprising of the Muhaajireen, the Ansaar, the Aslam tribe, the Ghifaar tribe, the Juhayna tribe and the Banu Sulaym tribe. They led with horses and (were so fast that) they reached Marruz Zahraan (close to Makkah) without the Quraysh even knowing about them. The Quraysh sent Hakeem bin
Tabraani. Haythami (Vol.6 Pg.170) has commented on the chain of narrators.
